title: Section cochain identifications respect the Hom differential with independent coefficient universe
statement: For a ringed site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], commutative ring sheaf R, object U and arbitrary module-sheaf cochain complexes L,I [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], let S be sections at U of their sheaf Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex], res restriction to U and π its chosen projections. Suppose additive equivalences e_n from S.X n to external degree-n cochains are given, and each component at p,q with p+n=q and localized W equals the evaluated projection π(L,I,n,p,q) applied to the section. Then for all integers i,j with i+1=j and all x in S.X i, e_j(S.d i j x)=δ i j(e_i x), where δ is Mathlib external Hom differential. No cycles or homology conclusion is assumed or asserted. This universe-general form takes C : Type u with Category v and coefficient/module universe max u v r, for arbitrary r; assume abelian-group sheafification and its locally bijective characterization on the original site. It uses the same sheaves, restriction, Hom complex, differentials, and induced maps as the original source statement.

proof.text: Work with objects in Type u, arrows in Type v, and coefficient rings and modules in Type (max u v r). Use the existing siteAbelianHasSheafify and siteAbelianWEqualsLocallyBijective instances on the slice whenever an abelian or exactness instance is needed. All these instances are proved, and the given base-site instances are retained.

For p+j=q, use the differential projection identity of homComplex_projections_exists with q′=p+i and p′=p+1. Evaluate at U and at W, preserving subtraction and integer multiplication. Internal Hom pre- and postcomposition become composition with the restricted complex differentials.

Substitute the hypothesized component formulas for e_i and e_j. The external differential formula δ_v uses j.negOnePow on the second summand; from j=i+1 derive j.negOnePow=-i.negOnePow. Thus both component maps agree. Extensionality of module-sheaf morphisms and cochains concludes. At i=0 this is d_I f-f d_L; at i=-1 it is d_I f+f d_L, and zero complexes give zero on both sides.
